expr: (list (condition-case e (substring "abcdef" 7) (args-out-of-range (cdr e))) (condition-case e (substring "abcdef" 4 2) (args-out-of-range (cdr e))) (condition-case e (substring "abcdef" 0 99) (args-out-of-range (cdr e))))
note: kg CLAMPS where Emacs RAISES, in all three directions, and the case is written to catch the condition so its DATA is the value rather than a symbol the runner would compare and kg would never produce. Emacs answers (("abcdef" 7 nil) ("abcdef" 4 2) ("abcdef" 0 99)) -- args-out-of-range with the offending string first, a nil END reported as nil. kg raises nothing and the `condition-case` returns the clamped substrings, ("" "" "abcdef"): a start past the end gives the empty string, a reversed pair gives the empty string, and an end past the end gives the whole string.
